t: Section 637a(a) of title 10, United States Code, is amended by inserting “separation or” after “provided for the”.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment that inserts the words "separation or" into 10 U.S.C. 637a(a), a provision on military officer personnel matters. There is no tempting participation reading: it involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.

opus.w: This section only changes the wording of a statute by adding "separation or" to 10 U.S.C. 637a(a). It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. Nothing in the text makes a 'Yes' reading plausible.

There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. Nothing here even looks like participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment to the United States Code, inserting specific words into an existing statute. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory committees, or coordination with non-federal entities. The text describes a legislative change, not a participatory mechanism.
qwen_chat.s: Section 637a(a) of title 10, United States Code, is amended by inserting “separation or” after “provided for the”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that amending a statute regarding "separation" implies a process involving employees or the public, but the text itself is merely a legislative amendment instruction. It does not describe any procedure for consultation, hearing, or input from outside parties. It simply changes the wording of a legal provision.
